pr_title: Cancel queued activities if AbortOnResupply is set.
pr_body:
This PR aims to fix #17525 by recreating the behaviour from `release-20190314` for both regular attacks and attack moves. This is a hack, but IMO not significantly worse than the rest of `AbortOnResupply`.

This is simple enough to also pick to the hotfix, if not rejected for being awful.

Fixes #17525.
Fixes #17249.
pr_comments:
This looks like it would trigger the bug where activities go directly from queued to canceling. That would need to be fixed first, which would put this beyond the scope of a hotfix, I think.

Perhaps a less hacky solution would be to always return false after queueing `ReturnToBase` and then calling `Cancel(self)` on the next tick (i.e. if `returnToBase == true && attackAircraft.Info.AbortOnResupply`).

> Perhaps a less hacky solution would be...

It is slightly more complicated than this because we also need to suppress the target lines for the later activities. This will need some more work to solve the `CurrentActivity` issue that @abcdefg30 found on IRC - if there isn't a simple solution that fixes both issues then we can go back to the drawing board for next + 1.

> This looks like it would trigger the bug where activities go directly from queued to canceling.

A possible work around could be to call `Cancel()` on the `FlyAttack`, which will then null out `NextActivity` and avoid queued cancellation bug. We then queue the RTB child activity, which should be able to run to completion because it didn't see the cancellation request.
Updated. This should fix the issues above, but means that the RTB target line is no longer shown. I'm not sure whether this could be considered an acceptable tradeoff?

I think this PR is a conceptual mistake and believe it is based on wrong assumptions. There is no gameplay expectation for AbortOnResupply - players don't know this attribute and should not need to. All they know is behavior they observed ingame, and this is what they base their expectations and assumptions on. I disagree with the assumption of this PR that the concept of explicit vs. implicit orders has any meaning for players and believe introducing this distinction in unit behavior will not be understood by everyone and be perceived as inconsistency.

I think it is a mistake to look at #17525 as an isolated regression. The underlying issue there and in the related issues is the inconsistency of AbortOnResupply - that setting the attribute to true does not do what name and description indicate, which is to abort activity on resupplying. Doing this consequently would solve all the problems without the need for any hacks. Yes, AbortOnResupply: true would mean that things get aborted when the unit resupplies, queued orders includes. Set it to false if you dont like that behavior.

You're trying to combine the benefits of both values for the attribute. That makes the attribute superfluous, confusing and inconsistent. So this PR does not fix the inconsistency root cause but helps establishing it. That's why I think it should not even be considered as a short-time hotfix patch.

I don't really understand your argument to be honest - there is indeed no expectation on that specific named flag, but there is an expectation in the way that units behave, which is what that flag controls. The activity rework made an unexpected change to these behaviours, and this PR aims to correct that.

> The activity rework made an unexpected change to these behaviours, and this PR aims to correct that.

It wasn't unexpected or unintentional though (at least not to me). Also, keep in mind that the behaviour on the previous release was exactly the same as on the current release ... if the queued order was given while the aircraft was on it's way back to base. So this isn't actually recreating the behaviour from previous release.

It's also pretty bad UX to let the player queue orders (and provide visual feedback for them) only to unpredictably drop them at some point halfway through. The simple fact that you can queue orders at all makes the `AbortOnResupply` behaviour completely counter to naive expectations. Indeed, players don't know about the `AbortOnResupply` flag (nor should they care), so this just comes across as a bug.

Ultimately, `AbortOnResupply` and order queueing are just completely at odds with eachother. Either disallow order queueing for airplanes or drop `AbortOnResupply`.

> Ultimately, `AbortOnResupply` and order queueing are just completely at odds with eachother. Either disallow order queueing for airplanes or drop `AbortOnResupply`.

This is at odds with the fact that all the C&C games that used `AbortOnResupply`-like logic, and several of them supported both Attack Move and queuing. To that end, I loaded up the three games I have at hand (It would be good if someone could fill in the Generals/ZH behaviour):
* RA2 supports both order queuing and attack move for vehicles, but neither for aircraft. Disappointing but not surprising considering the limitations of the engine.
* C&C3 and RA3 both RTB and cancel the current attack plus queued activities when running out of ammo during a standard attack.
* C&C3 doesn't RTB when running out of ammo during an attack move. Aircraft continue moving to the targeted location, then continue with any queued orders.
* The build of RA3 distributed through origin suffers from (what must be) a bug very similar to #17525 for only attack moves: units RTB and cancel the attack move, but then take off and start the next queued activity.

The primary action of an attack move order is to move to a location. My initial thought was that returning to base and then flying back to continue the activity was the solution here, but C&C3's solution also works.

I have pushed an update that fixes the initial set of hacks and implements an option to select between the C&C3 behaviour, and what I assume was supposed to be the RA3 behaviour (i.e. RTB during attack move and then canceling the queue). Unfortunately, this latter case requires a new pair of hacks that could be dropped if we are happy to support only the C&C3 behaviour.

This seems like a reasonable compromise between the different viewpoints given in #17525 and the desire to minimize code hacks here. It unfortunately makes for a larger PR due to the `GetAttackActivity` argument changes.

> C&C3 and RA3 both RTB and cancel the current attack plus queued activities when running out of ammo during a standard attack.

Are you sure about this? I already checked the behaviour in C&C3 and I found that airplanes do continue with their attack after rearming.
It may depend on patch version or C&C3 vs KW, but yes I tested it multiple times to confirm. They show the target lines to the old target, but never take off to act on them.

This was in KW. maybe what you saw has to do with losing visibility?

EDIT: It's the same in Tiberium Wars. They continue with their attack after rearming (when force-attacking your own units at least), but they seem to get stuck when chaining multiple attacks against enemy buildings (yet still show the target lines). I'm not yet sure whether the difference is due to force-attack or due to losing visibility. You can't queue multiple force-attacks (in fact it seems you can't combine any modifier) in C&C3 at all; also, attack orders are disabled when the aircraft is on it's way back to base. In any case, showing target lines, but not acting is definitely bogus so C&C3 cannot really be held up as an exemplar.

> Either disallow order queueing for airplanes or drop `AbortOnResupply`.

In addition to what @pchote said, the former would certainly cause a HUGE backlash from the player base after we just added/fixed queue support for nearly everything, while the latter would cause an uproar from modders (as it would make pre-C&C3 behavior impossible).

> (It would be good if someone could fill in the Generals/ZH behaviour)

Tested Generals ZH just now, but unless I overlooked something, the only kind of queueing it seems to have is a simple waypoint mode enabled by holding Alt, and it doesn't seem to support anything else than move commands (for both ground and air units).

On the general concept:
I feel at least part of the issue about `AbortOnResupply` is that a simple boolean isn't sufficient to cover all cases of behavior players and modders may want support for.
In my opinion this PR minus the `ResupplyDuringAttackMove`² field is good enough for prep (²once we've decided on the default behavior for RA, we should hardcode this for prep as to not introduce a field that might already be dropped again during the evolution of the bleed PR or a follow-up). 
But for Next+1 (or Next+2 if we can't decide on an approach before we branch of prep-next), I think we should consider refactoring `AbortOnResupply` more thoroughly, maybe into a `CancelOrderQueueOnResupplyOn` flag list with flags like `AttackMove`, `NormalAttack`, `ForceAttack` and so on.

Updated again:
 * Removed `ResupplyDuringAttackMove` and associated code hacks.
 * Implemented a proper fix to queued activity cancellation.

It turns out that the `TransformsInto*` traits all rely on canceling `NextActivity` directly, so we do need the proper fix for that rather than a local workaround here.

> I don't really understand your argument to be honest - there is indeed no expectation on that specific named flag, but there is an expectation in the way that units behave, which is what that flag controls. 

Yes, and them behaving differently depending on the context of the RTB order (explicitly/implicitly ordered) is bad bc it's inconsistent Continuing attack-moves after resupplying is also bad as it *encourages* a lazy playstyle of ordering a unit once and then let the game play itself. I don't like this but the important point is that it won't work - air units die in most cases when moving across the battlefield autonomously. It punishes the players who are willing to micro their units instead of replacing the aircraft because you have to cancel any attack-moves manually. This is how people work around it.

> The activity rework made an unexpected change to these behaviours, and this PR aims to correct that.

The "unexpected change" was the PR 26 days after the PR in which people agreed on to cancel orders / attack-moves when AOR=true. The change was indeed unexpected but in the meaning of contradictory. But it was not unintentional. And the implications for queued orders have also been raised before https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/16660#issuecomment-502454483.
Implementing the C&C3-style attack-move resolved your concern.

> It is slightly more complicated than this because we also need to suppress the target lines for the later activities.

The proper way to solve that would be to reintroduce the `IsTerminal` parameter that was cut from #16549 because we thought it wouldn't be needed anywhere. I don't think we should ever try to cancel `NextActivity` directly.

> I don't think we should ever try to cancel `NextActivity` directly.

* How do we prevent this? The current situation where the engine allows it to be called but then maybe crashes later isn't good enough.
* How do we solve the `TransformsInto*` cases that also need this?
It looks like this will also fix #17249, so updated the PR description.

comments:
This is a case of 

> Testing in #16584 uncovered a fairly nasty edge case in the activity state plumbing. I'm not sure whether it makes sense to fix it here, or in its own PR.
>
> If you queue a child activity and then cancel it before it can tick it will go directly from `ActivityState.Queued` to `ActivityState.Canceling`. This allows it to tick without `OnFirstRun` ever being called, which breaks a lot of assumptions!

_Originally posted by @pchote in https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/16481#issuecomment-498855282_

This would normally have been caught by https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/blob/060ea80ca41855b93666bdad386cb96976bbf10a/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Activities/Move/Move.cs#L162-L163 except the unit (a medic in this case) was indeed in a tunnel. This allows the rest of `Tick` to run without `OnFirstRun`, which, unsurprisingly, breaks horribly.

We could bodge a way around this by setting a flag in `OnFirstRun` and then making sure we always return if that has not been set. I would prefer it if we could instead fix the `Activity` plumbing properly so we wouldn't call `Tick` at all.

This issue exists in principle on the current prep branch, but we don't use tunnels in RA/TD/D2k so we should defer this to Next + 1.

review_comments: Queuing this as a non-child activity in the branch above should fix the target line issue. Otherwise (and IMO preferred), we need to expose a way for activities in the canceling state to opt in to drawing target lines.

Queuing this as a non-child activity in the branch above should fix the target line issue. Otherwise (and IMO preferred), we need to expose a way for activities in the canceling state to opt in to drawing target lines.
